blocks.html:
The importance of being playful

Free play makes us better adjusted, smarter and less stressed

A While it has long been recognized that play affords benefits that last through adulthood, psychologists in the US are now becoming concerned that lack of play could actually be harming their country's kids. In the past, few children grew up without ample free-play time. But youngsters' leisure hours are now filled with structured activities such as music lessons and sports. Kids play soccer, Scrabble and saxophone – so why are experts worried that these activities are eating into free play? Most games are fun and sources of learning experiences – fostering group cohesion, for instance, says educational psychologist Anthony Pellegrini. But, Pellegrini explains, “games have predetermined rules - set up in advance and followed. Play, on the other hand, does not have rules, so affords more creative responses. Children initiate and create free play, and use their imagination to try out new activities and roles.”

B Perhaps most crucially, play helps us develop strong social skills. “You don't become socially competent via teachers telling you how to behave,” Pellegrini says. “Kids learn those skills by interacting with peers, learning what is and isn't acceptable. They want this thing to keep going, so they're willing to 'go the extra mile' to accommodate their playmates' desires. Keeping things friendly requires communication – arguably the most valuable social skill of all. Play among peers is the most important in this regard.” Studies show that children use more sophisticated language when playing with other children than when playing with adults. In pretend play, for instance, they have to communicate about something that's not physically present, so they have to use complicated language to communicate what it is that they're trying to say,” Pellegrini explains.

C If play helps children become socialized, then lack of play should impede social development – and research suggests that it does. A study of children in Michigan revealed that kids who enrolled in play-oriented preschools were more socially adjusted later in life – and less likely to commit a felony or be suspended from work – than kids who attended play-free preschools where they were constantly instructed by teachers.

D A 2003 study even suggests that play promotes emotional and social development in animals. Researchers allowed thirteen rats to play freely with companions for three and a half days, and kept fourteen others isolated for the same period. Examination revealed that the brains of the rats which had played contained much higher levels of BDNF a protein that stimulates the growth of new neurons than those of the animals that had not. "I think play is the major mechanism whereby higher regions of the brain get socialized,” says neuroscientist Jaak Panksepp, who co-authored the study.

E Research also suggests that imaginative play is critical for children's emotional health, as it enables them to work through anxiety. In a 1984 study, researchers assessed the anxiety levels of seventy-four children on their first day of preschool. They labeled each child as either “anxious” or “not anxious”, then randomly split the kids into groups. Half were escorted to rooms full of toys, where they played for 15 minutes; the other half listened to a teacher tell a story for 15 minutes. Afterward, their levels were assessed again. The anxiety levels of the anxious kids who had played had dropped by more than twice as much compared with the anxious kids who had listened to the story.

F Results of animal studies support these views. In 2008, neuroscientist Stephen Siviy put rats into a chamber and exposed them to a collar previously worn by a cat, making them visibly anxious. Later, the chamber was cleaned to remove the cat odor, and the rats were put back without the collar. They immediately became anxious again, probably because they associated the space with the cat. The researchers then introduced another rat one that had never been exposed to the collar and was not afraid – and it began playing with one of the rats. “Shortly thereafter, the first rat relaxed and became calm," says Siviy, “suggesting that play helped lessen its anxiety."

G Play even appears to make kids smarter. In a classic study, researchers told a group of preschool children to play freely with some common objects such as paper towels, a screwdriver, a wooden board and paper clips. Another group was asked to imitate an experimenter using the objects in common ways. A third set was told to sit and draw whatever they wanted, without seeing the objects. After 10 minutes, the researchers asked the children to come up with ideas for how one of the objects could be used. The kids who had played with the objects named, on average, three times as many nonstandard, creative uses for the objects as those in either of the other two groups did, suggesting that play fosters imaginative thinking.

H A later animal study produced similar results. Experimenters isolated young rats during the development period when they would have most frequently played. The researchers taught these rats, and a group that had been allowed to play without constraints, to pull a rubber ball out of the way to get a food treat. A few days later they switched the setup so the rats would have to push the same ball to get the treat. Compared with the isolated rats, the ones which had played proved to be far more adept at solving problems. “Play is like a kaleidoscope,” says evolutionary biologist Marc Bekoff, “in that it is random and creative. It encourages flexibility and creativity that may, in the future, be advantageous in unexpected situations or new environments. And in the absence of play, children miss vital learning experiences.”

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–H, in boxes 14–18 on your answer sheet.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

ABCDEFGH
14 reference to how play can develop children's verbal skills
15 mention of a change in the amount of free play children engage in
16 an account of some research indicating that free play stimulates children's creativity
17 evidence of the link between antisocial behaviour and a lack of free play
18 a comparison between free play and other forms of play

Look at the following statements about free play (Questions 19–22) and the list of researchers below.

Match each statement with the correct researcher, A, B, C or D.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

19 It encourages children to take other people's wishes into account.

20 It can serve to relieve stress.

21 It prepares children for dealing with unpredictable situations.

22 It is less useful for children when adults are involved.

List of researchers
A Anthony Pellegrini
B Jaak Panksepp
C Stephen Siviy
D Marc Bekoff

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Animal research into the value of play

In studies researching links between play and social learning, experiments analysing protein levels in the 23 of rats noted significant differences between rats which had played and those which had not.

In another study, rats made distressed by an object smelling of a 24 experienced a noticeable reduction in their 25 levels after they had been allowed to play.

A further experiment, in which rats had to move a 26 in order to reach a reward, indicated that rats deprived of play were less skilled at dealing with problems.

meta.title: The importance of being playful 玩耍的重要性

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 尽管人们早就认识到玩耍带来的好处可以延续到成年，但美国的心理学家现在开始担心缺乏玩耍实际上可能正在伤害他们国家的孩子。过去，很少有孩子在没有充足自由玩耍时间的情况下成长。但如今年轻人的休闲时间被音乐课和体育等结构化活动填满了。孩子们踢足球、玩拼字游戏、吹萨克斯——那么为什么专家们担心这些活动正在侵蚀自由玩耍呢？教育心理学家Anthony Pellegrini说，大多数游戏都是有趣的，也是学习经验的来源——例如培养群体凝聚力。但Pellegrini解释说，“游戏有预定的规则——提前设定并遵循。另一方面，玩耍没有规则，因此能提供更多创造性的回应。孩子们发起和创造自由玩耍，用他们的想象力尝试新的活动和角色。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 也许最关键的是，玩耍帮助我们发展强大的社交技能。Pellegrini说：“你不是通过老师告诉你如何行为来获得社交能力的。孩子们通过与同龄人互动来学习这些技能，了解什么是可以接受的，什么是不可以接受的。他们希望这个活动继续下去，所以他们愿意'多走一英里'来满足玩伴的愿望。保持友好需要沟通——可以说这是所有社交技能中最有价值的。在这方面，同龄人之间的玩耍是最重要的。”研究表明，孩子们在与其他孩子玩耍时使用的语言比与成年人玩耍时更复杂。例如，在假装玩耍中，他们必须交流一些不在物理上存在的东西，所以他们必须使用复杂的语言来交流他们想表达的内容，Pellegrini解释道。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 如果玩耍帮助孩子社会化，那么缺乏玩耍应该会阻碍社会发展——研究表明确实如此。密歇根州的一项儿童研究显示，进入以游戏为导向的幼儿园的孩子在以后的生活中社会适应能力更强——不太可能犯重罪或被停职——比那些在没有玩耍的幼儿园、持续被老师指导的孩子。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 2003年的一项研究甚至表明玩耍促进了动物的情感和社会发展。研究人员让13只老鼠与同伴自由玩耍三天半，并将另外14只老鼠隔离相同的时间。检查发现，玩耍过的老鼠大脑中含有的BDNF——一种刺激新神经元生长的蛋白质——水平远高于没有玩耍过的动物。神经科学家Jaak Panksepp说：“我认为玩耍是大脑更高区域社会化的主要机制，”他是这项研究的合著者。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 研究还表明，想象力游戏对儿童的情感健康至关重要，因为它使他们能够克服焦虑。在1984年的一项研究中，研究人员在幼儿园的第一天评估了74名儿童的焦虑水平。他们将每个孩子标记为“焦虑”或“不焦虑”，然后随机将孩子们分成几组。一半被护送到满是玩具的房间，玩耍15分钟；另一半听老师讲故事15分钟。之后，再次评估他们的水平。玩耍的焦虑儿童的焦虑水平下降幅度是听故事的焦虑儿童的两倍多。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 动物研究的结果支持这些观点。2008年，神经科学家Stephen Siviy将老鼠放入一个腔室，让它们接触之前被猫戴过的项圈，使它们明显焦虑。后来，腔室被清理以去除猫的气味，老鼠被放回时没有项圈。它们立即再次变得焦虑，可能是因为它们将这个空间与猫联系起来。然后研究人员引入了另一只从未接触过项圈且不害怕的老鼠——它开始与其中一只老鼠玩耍。Siviy说：“此后不久，第一只老鼠放松下来变得平静，这表明玩耍有助于减轻其焦虑。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 玩耍甚至似乎让孩子更聪明。在一项经典研究中，研究人员让一组幼儿园儿童自由玩耍一些常见物品，如纸巾、螺丝刀、木板和回形针。另一组被要求模仿实验者以常见方式使用这些物品。第三组被告知坐下画他们想画的任何东西，不看这些物品。10分钟后，研究人员要求孩子们想出这些物品可以如何使用的主意。玩耍过这些物品的孩子平均说出的非标准、创造性的用途是其他两组中任何一组的三倍，这表明玩耍培养了想象力思维。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph H
passageNotes.text: 后来的一项动物研究产生了类似的结果。实验者在幼鼠最常玩耍的发育期间将它们隔离。研究人员教会这些老鼠以及一组被允许无约束玩耍的老鼠，把一个橡胶球移开来获得食物奖励。几天后他们改变了设置，使老鼠必须推同一个球来获得奖励。与隔离的老鼠相比，玩耍过的老鼠在解决问题方面要熟练得多。进化生物学家Marc Bekoff说：“玩耍就像一个万花筒，因为它是随机的和创造性的。它鼓励灵活性和创造力，这在未来可能在意外情况或新环境中具有优势。而在缺乏玩耍的情况下，孩子们错过了至关重要的学习体验。”

items.text:
（1）题目 14：reference to how play can develop children’s verbal skills
题目翻译：提到玩耍如何培养儿童的语言表达能力。
答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，末两句
原文：Studies show that children use more sophisticated language when playing with other children than when playing with adults.
译文：研究表明，孩子与其他孩子玩耍时使用的语言，比与成人玩耍时更复杂。

解析：more sophisticated language 直接说明同伴玩耍能够发展更复杂的语言能力，因此选 B。

（2）题目 15：mention of a change in the amount of free play children engage in
题目翻译：提到儿童参与自由玩耍的时间发生了变化。
答案：A
定位：正文 A 段，第2至3句
原文：In the past, few children grew up without ample free-play time. But youngsters’ leisure hours are now filled with structured activities such as music lessons and sports.
译文：过去，很少有孩子在缺少充足自由玩耍时间的情况下长大；但如今，孩子的空闲时间被音乐课和体育等结构化活动占满。

解析：In the past 与 now 形成时间对照，说明自由玩耍时间由充足变少，因此选 A。

（3）题目 16：an account of some research indicating that free play stimulates children’s creativity
题目翻译：描述一项表明自由玩耍能激发儿童创造力的研究。
答案：G
定位：正文 G 段，后半部分
原文：The kids who had played with the objects named, on average, three times as many nonstandard, creative uses for the objects as those in either of the other two groups did, suggesting that play fosters imaginative thinking.
译文：玩过这些物品的孩子平均提出的非常规、创造性用途，是另外两组的三倍，这表明玩耍能促进想象性思维。

解析：实验结果中的 creative uses 和 imaginative thinking 直接对应 stimulates children’s creativity，因此选 G。

（4）题目 17：evidence of the link between antisocial behaviour and a lack of free play
题目翻译：证明反社会行为与缺少自由玩耍之间存在联系。
答案：C
定位：正文 C 段，末句
原文：kids who enrolled in play-oriented preschools were more socially adjusted later in life – and less likely to commit a felony or be suspended from work – than kids who attended play-free preschools
译文：就读于以玩耍为导向的幼儿园的孩子，长大后社会适应更好，也更少犯罪或被停职；相比之下，另一组就读于不提供玩耍的幼儿园。

解析：play-free 与更差的社会适应、犯罪或停职相联系，构成缺少玩耍与反社会行为之间的证据，因此选 C。

（5）题目 18：a comparison between free play and other forms of play
题目翻译：把自由玩耍与其他形式的玩耍进行比较。
答案：A
定位：正文 A 段，末四句
原文：games have predetermined rules – set up in advance and followed. Play, on the other hand, does not have rules, so affords more creative responses.
译文：游戏有预先设定并遵守的规则；而自由玩耍没有规则，因此能够产生更多创造性反应。

解析：原文用 on the other hand 对比有固定规则的 games 与无规则的 free play，因此选 A。

items.text:
（1）题目 19：It encourages children to take other people’s wishes into account.
题目翻译：自由玩耍会鼓励孩子考虑他人的意愿。
答案：A
定位：正文 B 段，第3至4句
原文：They want this thing to keep going, so they’re willing to ‘go the extra mile’ to accommodate their playmates’ desires.
译文：为了让玩耍继续，孩子愿意多做一些，去迁就玩伴的愿望。

解析：accommodate their playmates’ desires 对应考虑他人的意愿；这段观点由 Anthony Pellegrini 提出，因此选 A。

（2）题目 20：It can serve to relieve stress.
题目翻译：自由玩耍可以帮助缓解压力。
答案：C
定位：正文 F 段，末句
原文：Shortly thereafter, the first rat relaxed and became calm,” says Siviy, “suggesting that play helped lessen its anxiety.
译文：不久后，第一只老鼠放松并平静下来；Siviy 说，这表明玩耍帮助减轻了它的焦虑。

解析：relaxed、became calm 与 lessen its anxiety 都对应缓解压力；说话者是 Stephen Siviy，因此选 C。

（3）题目 21：It prepares children for dealing with unpredictable situations.
题目翻译：自由玩耍能让孩子为应对不可预知的情况做好准备。
答案：D
定位：正文 H 段，末三句
原文：It encourages flexibility and creativity that may, in the future, be advantageous in unexpected situations or new environments.
译文：它能培养灵活性和创造力，而这些能力将来在意外情境或新环境中可能很有优势。

解析：unexpected situations or new environments 对应不可预知的情况；该观点来自 Marc Bekoff，因此选 D。

（4）题目 22：It is less useful for children when adults are involved.
题目翻译：当成人参与时，玩耍对孩子的作用较小。
答案：A
定位：正文 B 段，末两句
原文：Studies show that children use more sophisticated language when playing with other children than when playing with adults.
译文：研究显示，孩子与其他孩子玩耍时使用的语言，比与成人玩耍时更复杂。

解析：同伴玩耍带来的语言收益高于与成人玩耍，说明成人参与时效果较弱；该观点来自 Anthony Pellegrini，因此选 A。

解析：unexpected situations or new environments 对应不可预知的情况；该观点来自 Marc Bekoff，因此选 D。

（4）题目 22：It is less useful for children when adults are involved.
题目翻译：当成人参与时，玩耍对孩子的作用较小。
答案：A
定位：正文 B 段，末两句
原文：Studies show that children use more sophisticated language when playing with other children than when playing with adults.
译文：研究显示，孩子与其他孩子玩耍时使用的语言，比与成人玩耍时更复杂。

解析：同伴玩耍带来的语言收益高于与成人玩耍，说明成人参与时效果较弱；该观点来自 Anthony Pellegrini，因此选 A。

items.text:
（1）题目 23：In studies researching links between play and social learning, experiments analysing protein levels in the ________ of rats noted significant differences between rats which had played and those which had not. In another study, rats made distressed by an object smelling of a ________ experienced a noticeable reduction in their ________ levels after they had been allowed to play. A further experiment, in which rats had to move a ________ in order to reach a reward, indicated that rats deprived of play were less skilled at dealing with problems.
题目翻译：实验检测老鼠________中的蛋白质水平，发现玩过和没玩过的老鼠存在显著差异。
答案：brains
定位：正文 D 段，第3句
原文：Examination revealed that the brains of the rats which had played contained much higher levels of BDNF
译文：检测显示，玩耍过的老鼠大脑中含有高得多的 BDNF。

解析：题干的 protein levels in the ___ of rats 对应 brains of the rats，因此填 brains。

（2）题目 24：In studies researching links between play and social learning, experiments analysing protein levels in the ________ of rats noted significant differences between rats which had played and those which had not. In another study, rats made distressed by an object smelling of a ________ experienced a noticeable reduction in their ________ levels after they had been allowed to play. A further experiment, in which rats had to move a ________ in order to reach a reward, indicated that rats deprived of play were less skilled at dealing with problems.
题目翻译：一种带有________气味的物体使老鼠感到不安。
答案：cat
定位：正文 F 段，第2句
原文：Siviy put rats into a chamber and exposed them to a collar previously worn by a cat, making them visibly anxious.
译文：Siviy 把老鼠放入箱中，让它们接触一条曾被猫戴过的项圈，使它们明显焦虑。

解析：题干已用 object 概括 collar，空格问气味来自什么动物；原文是 cat，因此填 cat。

（3）题目 25：In studies researching links between play and social learning, experiments analysing protein levels in the ________ of rats noted significant differences between rats which had played and those which had not. In another study, rats made distressed by an object smelling of a ________ experienced a noticeable reduction in their ________ levels after they had been allowed to play. A further experiment, in which rats had to move a ________ in order to reach a reward, indicated that rats deprived of play were less skilled at dealing with problems.
题目翻译：玩耍后，这些老鼠的________水平明显下降。
答案：anxiety
定位：正文 F 段，末句
原文：suggesting that play helped lessen its anxiety.
译文：这表明玩耍帮助减轻了它的焦虑。

解析：reduction 对应 lessen，题干已经给出 levels，空格应填被降低的状态 anxiety。

（4）题目 26：In studies researching links between play and social learning, experiments analysing protein levels in the ________ of rats noted significant differences between rats which had played and those which had not. In another study, rats made distressed by an object smelling of a ________ experienced a noticeable reduction in their ________ levels after they had been allowed to play. A further experiment, in which rats had to move a ________ in order to reach a reward, indicated that rats deprived of play were less skilled at dealing with problems.
题目翻译：老鼠必须移动一个________才能拿到奖励。
答案：ball
定位：正文 H 段，第3至4句
原文：The researchers taught these rats, and a group that had been allowed to play without constraints, to pull a rubber ball out of the way to get a food treat.
译文：研究人员教这些老鼠把一个橡胶球拉开，以便获得食物奖励。

解析：move 概括 pull ... out of the way，所移动的物体核心名词是 ball；rubber ball 超过一词限制。
